data.name: Jahir
data.gender_notes: Jahir is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The One Whose Glory is Radiant. The name Jahir carries the meaning “Glory, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Jahir usually hope their child will grow to embody glory, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for someone who is a beacon of light and glory, often used for scholars, leaders, and those with a strong desire to spread knowledge and wisdom
data.etymology: Jahir belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Glory, Radiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jahir total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_arabic.name: ظاهر
in_arabic.meaning: الظاهر بمعنى واضح و جلى و ظاهر للعيان
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم الظاهر من أسماء الله الحسنى، يعني الذي يظهر للجميع، ويعبر عن الوضوح والظهور، وقد ورد ذكره في القرآن الكريم في سورة الجمعة: هو الذي أرسل رسوله بالهدى و دين الحق ليظهره على الدين كله ولو كره المشركون

in_urdu.name: ظاہر
in_urdu.meaning: ظاہر کا مطلب واضح اور جلی ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: ظاہر ایک عربی نام ہے جس کا مطلب واضح اور ظاہر ہونے والا ہے، یہ اللہ کے ناموں میں سے ایک ہے جیسا کہ قرآن میں مذکور ہے، اور اسلامی تقالید میں اس کا بڑا دینی اور ثقافتی اہمیت ہے

in_hindi.name: ज़ाहिर
in_hindi.meaning: ज़ाहिर का अर्थ है स्पष्ट और जाहिर होने वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: ज़ाहिर एक अरबी नाम है जिसका अर्थ है स्पष्ट और जाहिर होने वाला, यह अल्लाह के नामों में से एक है जैसा कि कुरआन में उल्लेखित है, और इस्लामी परंपराओं में इसकी बड़ी धार्मिक और सांस्कृतिक महत्ता है

in_pashto.name: ظاهر
in_pashto.meaning: ظاهر د واضح او څرګند معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: ظاهر د عربي نوم دی چې د واضح او څرګند معنا لري، دا د الله تعالی یو نوم دی لکه څنګه چې په قرآن کې ياد شوی دی، او په اسلامي دودونو کې يې لوی مذهبي او کلتوري اهميت لري

in_english.name: Jahir
in_english.long_meaning: Jahir is an Arabic name derived from the root 'ظ-ه-ر' which means 'to appear' or 'to become manifest'. It is one of the names of Allah in Islam, signifying 'the one who appears' or 'the manifest'. The name Jahir holds significant spiritual and cultural importance in Islamic tradition, symbolizing clarity, visibility, and divine presence. Historically, it has been used across various Muslim cultures, reflecting its universal appeal and timeless relevance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jahir holds a rich cultural significance in the Islamic world. It is derived from the Arabic word "Jahara" which means "shine" or "radiate". This name was often used for incredible structures and brilliant architectural designs created throughout Islamic history. For instance, the Taj Mahal in India is a famous example of a 'Jahar' as it is a structure of great brilliance and radiance.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Jahir carries a profound meaning. It signifies the innate desire within each individual to illuminate their inner selves and radiate this light in the world around them. The name serves as a reminder for every believer to strive towards achieving self-improvement and spiritual enlightenment. By embracing this name, one is acknowledging their innate potential to shine brightly like a star, and is encouraged to make their life a reflection of the divine glory radiant in their character and actions.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Glory, Radiant" symbolizes The One Whose Glory is Radiant. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Jahir serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of glory, radiant.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Jahir ibn Bukayr was a renowned scholar and historian in the Abbasid Caliphate, particularly known for his work 'Al-Jahiz on zoology and literature. His works provided a significant contribution to the development of Islamic sciences during the Golden Age of Islam.
historical_references.context: Abbasid Caliphate, Islamic sciences, zoology, literature, Golden Age of Islam

historical_references.reference: Jahir al-Iqbal was a prominent Sufi saint and poet in the Indian subcontinent during the medieval period. He is often referred to as 'Galandar Shah' and is famous for his poetry that expresses love and devotion towards God.
historical_references.context: Medieval period, Indian subcontinent, Sufi saint, poet, love and devotion towards God
